theorems.T1_fixed_integer_equivalence: For PCF4 public prefix L, gcd(G_N(L),N)=gcd(F_L,N), so a public-prefix query is a gcd probe against an N-independent integer.
theorems.T2_exact_amplification: If theta_N is the one-trial split probability under a public seed law and trials are independent, T trials split with probability 1-(1-theta_N)^T. If theta_N=0, amplification remains exactly zero.
theorems.T3_polynomial_prefix_balanced_zero_famil: For every polynomial prefix cap P(n), there are infinitely many balanced semiprimes N=pq such that gcd(F_L,N)=1 for every 1<=L<=P(n). Hence any randomized or adaptive PCF4 recurrence campaign confined to polynomial prefix lengths has worst-case split probability exactly zero.
theorems.T4_L_equals_N_cost: Under the frozen term-by-term recurrence, L=N requires at least N recurrence stages, hence Omega(N)=Omega(2^(n-1)) arithmetic stages before the final gcd, already worse than the square-root candidate-count scale.
theorems.T5_frozen_public_probe_fixed_support: The frozen quadratic and sixth-power public probes at seeds 0..63 are finite families of gcds against fixed integers f(s); therefore they also admit infinitely many semiprime zero-success inputs despite their finite benchmark success rates.
